title: Focused dynamic lens routing with fingerprinted selective reuse
summary: Add one dependency-neutral deterministic routing policy over the incumbent 26-lens signal engine; adapt Product, Design, Plan, and Evaluate to stage-specific focused routes; preserve complete dispositions, fail-closed overflow, authenticated expansion, per-lens evidence reuse, and zero lens workers in Build, Fix, and EM.

current_state.summary: The incumbent signal engine scores all 26 lenses as deep/light/n/a with an eight-deep cap and security/architecture floors. Product and Plan still use legacy strategy routing, Design forces only solution-design, automatic Review/Evaluate projects four or five sweep lenses, retry membership follows prior failures rather than canonical per-lens input changes, and the sealed zero-lens delivery mode currently suppresses Evaluate and EM together with Build/Fix. Existing ReviewKernel evidence, leases, native dispatch, storage, signing, and telemetry are retained.

alternatives.name: Shared pure policy with incumbent adapters
alternatives.description: Introduce one standard-library-only pure routing-policy module and keep current signal scoring, stage lifecycle, ReviewKernel provenance, signing, storage, and telemetry as consuming adapters.

gains: One deterministic disposition, cap, overflow, and fingerprint contract serves every routed stage
Reuses mature graph floors, scoped evidence views, leases, atomic collection, and native lifecycle enforcement
Keeps stage-specific evidence ownership explicit without copying an earlier route forward
costs: Requires a versioned compatibility reader for prior deep/light/n/a route history
Touches several stage adapters and gates even though the policy core is one module
Requires conservative per-lens relevance declarations before evidence may be reused
tradeoffs.revisit_when: A second independent router consumer needs non-Python execution or stage adapters cannot express their context without importing ReviewKernel internals.

alternatives.name: Independent policy in each stage
alternatives.description: Patch Product, Design, Plan, and Evaluate separately, keeping selection and evidence rules next to each stage gate.

gains: Small initial change in each individual stage
costs: Duplicates canonicalization, disposition validation, cap behavior, privacy, and fingerprint logic
Makes equal-input determinism across stages difficult to prove
Allows mandatory-risk and covered-by semantics to drift between gates
tradeoffs.revisit_when: The requirement is narrowed to one routed stage and cross-stage determinism is explicitly removed.

alternatives.name: Replace the signal engine and ReviewKernel
alternatives.description: Create a new router, evidence store, dispatcher, retry engine, and result collector around the new disposition vocabulary.

gains: No legacy route vocabulary inside the new implementation
A single greenfield data model from context through collection
costs: Discards incumbent graph floors, scoped views, host-observed leases, collection atomicity, and provenance
Creates a broad migration and regression surface unrelated to the requirement
Delays focused routing behind a full review-system replacement
tradeoffs.revisit_when: ReviewKernel provenance or storage is separately approved for replacement and a migration plan preserves every canonical evidence receipt.

decision: Select the shared pure policy because the approved behavior is one cross-stage invariant while context and execution remain stage-owned. A dependency-neutral core makes ordering, dispositions, overflow, fingerprints, and privacy mechanically identical; incumbent adapters retain proven scoring, authority, dispatch, and evidence collection. This is the smallest change that satisfies all ten acceptance criteria without a stage-local consistency gap or a ReviewKernel rewrite.

contracts.description: One policy version deterministically converts a validated stage context and 26 scored catalog rows into the smallest sufficient ordered focused route.
Every Product, Design, Plan, and Evaluate route has exactly one evidenced execute_deep, execute_light, covered_by, or not_applicable disposition for each of the 26 catalog lenses.
Only Product, Design, Plan, and Evaluate may execute selected lenses; Build, Fix, and EM prove zero lens-worker starts across every terminal lifecycle outcome.
A narrowly scoped signed capability may authorize one exact Plan/Evaluate route above four lenses without altering mandatory floors or general contract enforcement.
Immutable route and per-lens canonical input fingerprints bind selection, evidence reuse, invalidation, policy version, and catalog version.
Bounded redacted records expose stage, selected count and reasons, estimated/actual tokens, runtime, cache reuse, invalidation, terminal status, and route fingerprint.

closed_invariants: exactly one disposition for every catalog lens in catalog order
only execute_deep and execute_light rows appear in selected
covered_by targets one selected lens and coverage edges are acyclic
mandatory risk floors are applied before cap or deduplication
equal canonical context, catalog, and policy version produce byte-identical decision material

proposed_edges.reason: The incumbent dependency-neutral detector supplies complete scored rows and mandatory risk-floor evidence to the pure selector.
The catalog adapter projects existing scores into the canonical context and converts selected dispositions into dispatch briefs.
The pure policy owns deterministic stage selection, count rules, risk deduplication, and overflow refusal.
The pure policy validates the exact 26-row closed disposition ledger and selected-set conservation.
Product, Design, and Plan stage adapters build fresh stage-specific contexts and mechanically gate their artifacts.
ReviewKernel builds Evaluate context from the actual diff, impact, tests, and findings before minting any slot.
Loop dispatch confines lens execution to routed decision stages and emits zero-lens Build/Fix/EM authority.
Closed native lifecycle observations prove zero Taskplane lens starts for Build, Fix, and EM without suppressing Evaluate.
The control plane signs and verifies one target-, context-, lens-, cost-, expiry-, and policy-bound exceptional route action.
ReviewKernel seals route input, route decision, per-lens input fingerprints, reused results, leases, and new results as one conserved evidence set.
Fix-to-Evaluate comparison reuses only sealed passing evidence with an equal canonical per-lens input fingerprint.
The existing immutable usage ledger gains a closed bounded stage-route record for cost, runtime, reuse, invalidation, and terminal state.
Product authority records the complete routed-stage transparency and acceptance contract.
The Design Contract fixes the stage policies, boundaries, route schema, and rollout before implementation.
Plan maps the approved stage rules and every designed edge to dependency-aware implementation and validation tasks.
Unit and mutation tests reject missing, duplicate, unsupported, cyclic, and unevidenced dispositions.
Authority tests reject tampering, replay, expiry, stage/target mismatch, and any attempt to weaken mandatory floors.
Determinism and selective-invalidation tests mutate one, multiple, unchanged, and policy-version inputs.
Schema, bound, redaction, token, runtime, reuse, and invalidation telemetry tests prove complete privacy-safe records.
Role contracts explain which stages apply focused quick lenses and forbid Build/Fix nested lens execution.
The facade and harness route stage work without prompting users to select lenses.
Routing, catalog, state, configuration, and onboarding docs describe focused execution, overflow, reuse, and observability truthfully.
README product truth states the normal focused routes, 3–4 Plan/Evaluate bound, and separate explicit all-deep audit.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC-LR1: Product deterministically executes a minimum-sufficient focused route from goal, requirement, AC, domain, constraints, and product-risk evidence, emits all 26 dispositions, and never launches a normal full-catalog run; verify identical-input and product-risk mutation tests.
acceptance_map.design_element: contract:lens.focused-stage-routing; taskplane/lens_route_policy.py; Product context adapter in taskplane/loop.py
acceptance_map.validation: Run the Product identical-context determinism test, mutate product-risk evidence one field at a time, and assert complete 26-row dispositions with no breadth=all or full-catalog dispatch.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC-LR2: Design deterministically executes a minimum-sufficient focused route from approved requirement and proposed solution evidence, includes solution-design coverage, and emits findings, design changes, and all 26 dispositions; verify independent interface, trust-boundary, and rollback-risk mutations.
acceptance_map.design_element: contract:lens.focused-stage-routing; Design context adapter and Design Contract route evidence
acceptance_map.validation: Run the Design route test with independent interface, trust-boundary, and rollback-risk mutations; assert solution-design remains selected and every mutation changes only attributable decision evidence.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC-LR3: Every non-trivial Plan executes exactly three or four selected lenses with rationale and task-to-AC coverage; verify passing 3/4 cases and refusal of 2/5.
acceptance_map.design_element: contract:lens.focused-stage-routing; Plan route gate in taskplane/loop.py; plan/tasks.json route coverage
acceptance_map.validation: Run Plan fixtures with exactly three and four independent risks, then mutate selected counts to two and five and require the mechanical gate to refuse both.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC-LR4: Every non-trivial task or wave Evaluate executes exactly three or four lenses from actual diff, changed files, dependency impact, test evidence, and unresolved findings; verify material evidence changes alter the route.
acceptance_map.design_element: taskplane/review.py Evaluate adapter; contract:lens.focused-stage-routing; ReviewKernel slot conservation
acceptance_map.validation: Start ReviewKernel on frozen task and wave fixtures, assert three/four singleton selected slots, then independently mutate diff, impact, tests, and unresolved findings and verify attributable route-fingerprint changes.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC-LR5: Plan/Evaluate with more than four independent mandatory risks splits scope or refuses pending authenticated expanded-route approval listing extra lenses and cost; verify no silent drop and reject tampered approval.
acceptance_map.design_element: contract:authority.expanded-lens-route; overflow result in taskplane/lens_route_policy.py; signed action in taskplane/taskplane_lite.py
acceptance_map.validation: Inject five independent mandatory risks, prove zero dispatch and deterministic split/refusal, then verify only an exact signed route/cost capability succeeds while lens, cost, context, target, expiry, and signature mutations fail.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC-LR6: Product, Design, Plan, and Evaluate each emit exactly one internally consistent evidenced disposition for every catalog lens, and only execute_deep/execute_light launch workers; verify missing, duplicate, unsupported, and unevidenced rows fail closed.
acceptance_map.validation: Run the 26-row conservation test for all four stages and a mutation matrix covering missing, duplicate, unknown, unsupported, unevidenced, covered-by-cycle, and selected-set mismatches before dispatch.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC-LR7: A material Fix invalidates and reruns only lens evidence whose canonical fingerprint inputs changed while unchanged evidence is reused without launching a worker; verify single-input, multi-input, and unchanged cases.
acceptance_map.design_element: resource:review.route-fingerprint; taskplane/review_retry.py per-lens comparison; taskplane/review.py reused/new evidence conservation
acceptance_map.validation: Run single-input, multiple-input, and unchanged Fix fixtures; assert exact invalidated lenses receive leases, matching sealed pass evidence is reused, and unchanged input launches zero duplicate lens workers.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC-LR8: Equal canonical inputs and policy version produce the same ordered route, dispositions, and fingerprint for all routed stages; verify repeats, key-order variance, relevant-input change, and policy-version change.
acceptance_map.validation: Repeat Product/Design/Plan/Evaluate contexts with permuted mapping keys and stable semantic lists, then mutate one relevant input and policy version; assert equal bytes for equivalent contexts and different route fingerprints for material changes.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC-LR9: Each route records stage, selected count, reasons, estimated/actual tokens, runtime, cache reuse, and invalidation cause with bounded redaction; verify schema completeness and privacy behavior.
acceptance_map.design_element: resource:telemetry.lens-route; taskplane/dispatch_telemetry.py closed route telemetry record
acceptance_map.validation: Validate complete terminal telemetry for pass/fail/cancel/interruption/handoff, enforce 512-byte reasons and 128-KiB artifact bounds, and inject secrets, absolute paths, workstation identity, and raw diff text to prove redaction/refusal.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC-LR10: Successful, failed, cancelled, interrupted, and handed-off Build/Fix attempts launch zero lens workers, with lens execution confined to Product, Design, Plan, and Evaluate; verify native-dispatch traces.
acceptance_map.design_element: contract:delivery.stage-lens-execution; taskplane/delivery_policy.py zero-lens lifecycle validator; taskplane/loop.py stage dispatch
acceptance_map.validation: Replay native start/terminal traces for successful, failed, cancelled, interrupted, and handed-off Build/Fix attempts and assert zero tp-lens starts; prove Evaluate focused slots remain allowed and EM remains synthesis-only.

quality_targets.threshold: at most 512 UTF-8 bytes and no absolute/private content

quality_targets.measure: native lens worker starts per non-trivial target
quality_targets.threshold: Product/Design minimum sufficient; Plan/Evaluate 3 or 4 absent signed expansion; Build/Fix/EM exactly 0

risks.risk: Stage adapters supply semantically different context for the same evidence and break determinism.
risks.mitigation: Use one closed context schema, canonical serializer, shared policy version, catalog fingerprint, cross-stage fixtures, and key-order mutation tests.

risks.risk: Risk deduplication marks two independent mandatory concerns as covered and silently narrows review.
risks.mitigation: Require explicit risk-group evidence, selected covering lens, acyclic coverage, mandatory-floor application before deduplication, and five-risk overflow mutation tests.

risks.risk: Evidence from before a Fix is reused against materially changed inputs.
risks.mitigation: Bind reuse to per-lens canonical input fingerprints, policy/catalog version, sealed passing result, and host provenance; default every uncertainty to invalidated.

risks.risk: Expanded-route authority becomes a generic bypass or can be replayed.
risks.mitigation: Use a closed signed capability bound to workspace, stage, target, context fingerprint, exact lenses, cost, expiry, policy, and one action id; never expose a general clear or floor override.

risks.risk: The existing zero-lens delivery authority continues to suppress Evaluate.
risks.mitigation: Separate Build/Fix/EM zero-lens validation from Evaluate routing and add positive Evaluate-dispatch plus negative Build/Fix/EM lifecycle tests.

risks.risk: Route evidence or telemetry leaks raw prompts, diffs, secrets, workstation identity, or absolute paths.
risks.mitigation: Persist bounded reason codes, repository-relative paths, pseudonymous targets, content hashes, closed schemas, and explicit privacy mutation tests.

risks.risk: Legacy route history is mistaken for current dispatch or reuse authority.
risks.mitigation: Keep a one-generation read-only renderer that cannot authorize dispatch/reuse and require focused-routing/v1 for every new gate.

failure_modes.mode: A stage context, disposition ledger, or selected set violates its closed schema.
failure_modes.recovery: The owning stage adapter emits routing_policy_unavailable, dispatches zero lens workers, and the stage owner corrects the named context or ledger before retrying the same target.

failure_modes.mode: Plan or Evaluate has more than four independent mandatory risks.
failure_modes.recovery: The planner/evaluator splits the target along the deterministic disjoint scopes, or the human supplies one exact signed expanded-route capability before dispatch.

failure_modes.mode: A Fix changes one or more canonical inputs for previously selected lens evidence.
failure_modes.recovery: ReviewKernel reuses only equal sealed pass fingerprints, mints new leases for every invalidated or newly selected lens, and refuses completion until their results collect.

failure_modes.mode: An expanded-route action is tampered, replayed, expired, or bound to another target/context.
failure_modes.recovery: The control-plane authority owner rejects it with zero dispatch; the orchestrator requests a new exact action only if the human still authorizes the same current route.

failure_modes.mode: A Taskplane lens worker starts during Build, Fix, or EM.
failure_modes.recovery: The loop blocks the stage gate, terminalizes the offending child contract, preserves the native trace, and reruns only after the stage dispatch is corrected.

failure_modes.mode: Immutable route or telemetry persistence fails before the stage pointer is updated.
failure_modes.recovery: The storage owner leaves the previous pointer authoritative, removes or quarantines the incomplete temporary object, and retries the atomic write without dispatching from partial evidence.

failure_modes.mode: Estimated or actual lens usage is absent, non-finite, negative, or exceeds its schema bound.
failure_modes.recovery: The telemetry owner marks the route incomplete, blocks terminal route accounting, and reconstructs usage only from the sealed native receipt; it never guesses a value.

alerts: Block the current stage immediately when lens_route_validation_failure or route_artifact_write_failure is emitted.
Require human-visible overflow handling when lens_route_overflow is emitted and no deterministic split is available.
Block Build/Fix/EM completion on any build_fix_lens_start_violation.
Surface repeated expanded_route_authority_rejection after two attempts for the same target fingerprint without weakening validation.
Fail the cost/reuse ratchet when lens_route_dispatch_count exceeds four without a valid expanded-route receipt or when unchanged evidence launches a worker.

rollout.strategy: Add focused-routing/v1 and its exhaustive unit/mutation tests first; wire Product/Design/Plan gates; wire Evaluate route/reuse while retaining read-only legacy history rendering; narrow zero-lens enforcement to Build/Fix/EM; add signed expansion, telemetry, skills/agents/docs; then run focused selectors, compatibility interpreters, Python 3.14 lint/strict types, packaged-plugin import smoke, strict graph verification, and the full Taskplane suite before final review.
rollout.rollback: Before release, revert the implementation commits. After focused-routing/v1 artifacts exist, restore the prior reader while retaining immutable route history and stop new routed stages as routing_policy_unavailable until an explicitly compatible policy is selected; never fall back automatically to full-catalog execution, zero-Evaluate execution, or rewritten evidence.

technical_debt.title: Remove legacy deep/light/n/a history reader
technical_debt.reason: One compatibility generation must render prior immutable review history without treating it as current authority.
technical_debt.follow_up: Remove after two consecutive released versions report zero legacy route reads; the reader must never authorize dispatch or evidence reuse.

python_runtime.execution_model: synchronous pure policy; existing stage owners retain cancellation, interruption, handoff, and child lifecycle control
python_runtime.mutable_shared_state: none in lens_route_policy.py; callers pass immutable values and storage mutations remain under incumbent atomic locks
python_runtime.free_threaded: safe by construction for the pure policy; no extension modules or GIL-dependent mutation are introduced
python_runtime.packaging: existing Taskplane plugin/package namespace; include lens_route_policy.py and verify a clean packaged-plugin import with no network access

visualization.reason: The stage execution boundary, overflow refusal, and Fix-to-Evaluate selective-reuse transition are easier to verify together as one state flow than as separate prose rules.

lens_evidence.evidence: Checked the exact R-0001 criteria against incumbent signal, loop, ReviewKernel, retry, authority, delivery-policy, telemetry, packaging, Python 3.14, and graph boundaries; compared three real approaches; verified every proposed module/edge traces to acceptance, a failure control, or a numeric quality target; made overflow, per-lens invalidation, zero-lens stages, rollback, storage atomicity, trust-boundary validation, and clean-package verification implementable without unresolved invention.
